**`ex-squarefree-sums-of-two-squares` (ai-generated construction) — verified by direct enumeration, not by trusting the proof.** Squarefree $n\le30$: $1,2,3,5,6,7,10,11,13,14,15,17,19,21,22,23,26,29,30$ — I enumerated all 30 and the list is exactly right (4, 8, 9, 12, 16, 18, 20, 24, 25, 27, 28 correctly excluded). Removing those with an odd prime factor in $\{3,7,11,19,23\}$ leaves $1,2,5,10,13,17,26,29$ — matches. All eight witnesses check ($1{+}0$, $1{+}1$, $1{+}4$, $1{+}9$, $4{+}9$, $1{+}16$, $1{+}25$, $4{+}25$) and every coordinate gcd is $1$. **No counterexample exists; I did not need to search beyond the finite range the Statement quantifies over.**

**Primitivity vs. representability.** The two characterisations are kept apart cleanly. `thm-sum-of-two-squares-characterisation` says *sum of two squares* and requires even $v_q$ for $q\equiv3$; `thm-primitive-sum-of-two-squares-characterisation` says *primitive* and requires $v_2(n)\le1$ **and** $q\nmid n$. No proof uses one to license the other. I spot-checked the criterion against $n=1,2,4,5,9,10,25,50,68,833$ — all agree. The sharpness of `cor-primitive-sums-of-two-squares-closed-under-products` is real: both factors even forces $v_2(mn)=2$, so the "unless" is not a defensive hedge.

**Degenerate instantiations, per item.** $n=0$ (excluded by "positive" in both characterisations; `cor-sums-of-two-squares-closed-under-products` step 3.1 handles the zero factor explicitly); $n=1$ (empty factorisation, $(1,0)$, and $\gcd(1,0)=1$ by the published convention at `def-common-divisor-and-gcd:41-52`, so it really is primitive); $n=2$; $a=0$ (primitivity is well-defined because $\gcd(x,0)=|x|$ and $\gcd(0,0)=0$ are both fixed on disk, line 59); $a=b$ (cannot be normalized, since normalization demands one odd and one even coordinate); exponent $0$ in `lem-two-square-representations-of-prime-powers` (both clauses hold, and $0$ is even); $j=0$ in its step 1.3 (the base case is argued, not skipped — $q^2\mid q$); $e=0$ in `lem-prime-one-mod-four-powers-…` (the two candidates are $(a,b)$ and $(a,-b)$, both primitive); $p=2$ in Thue ($h=1$, $|r|,|s|=1<\sqrt2$); empty factor list in `thm-primitive-…` step 3.1.

**$p=2$ and the odd-prime hypotheses.** `lem-prime-one-mod-four-powers-…` quantifies only over $p\equiv1$, and its consumer `thm-primitive-sum-of-two-squares-characterisation` does **not** silently extend it to $2$ — step 2.1 supplies $(1,1)$ for the factor $2$ by hand. `lem-three-mod-four-prime-dividing-two-square-sum` needs $q$ odd for [L1]/[F2]; $q\equiv3\pmod4$ delivers that, and all four consumers pass $q\equiv3$. `lem-thue-small-representatives` needs $p\nmid a$; `thm-fermat` step 1.3 establishes it from $(-1/p)=1$.

**Both directions of every iff.** `thm-fermat` (1.1 necessity for odd, 1.2 for $p=2$, 3.1 sufficiency); `thm-sum-of-two-squares-characterisation` (2.1 reverse, 3.1 forward, with the valuation-1 contradiction actually closing); `thm-primitive-…` (1.1+1.2 necessity, 3.1 sufficiency); `cor-squarefree-…` (1.1 criterion, 2.1 existence, 1.2 the separate "every representation is primitive" claim); `lem-two-square-representations-of-prime-powers` (1.2 even exponents, 1.3 odd exponents impossible).
